learning_outcomes.text: Students will be able to define relevant random events for a given random experiment and compute probabilities of simple and composite events.

Students will be able to check the independence of events, calculate conditional probabilities, and apply Bayes
y_x0019_ Theorem.

Students will compute probabilities, expected values, and variances of random variables using probability mass functions (PMF), probability density functions (PDF), and cumulative distribution functions (CDF).
Students will understand and utilize properties of well-known discrete and continuous probability distributions.

Students will analyze joint distributions to compute probabilities for events involving multiple random variables, derive marginal distributions, and determine the distributions of functions of two random variables.
Students will understand properties of random samples and the distributions of sample means and variances.

syllabus_topics: Bernoulli, binomial, Poisson, geometric, negative binomial random variables
Uniform, normal, exponential, Gamma random variables
Independent random variables and the distribution of their sums
assessment_rules: The final success grade is determined by the contribution of in-term activities and the final exam grade. The midterm examination contributes 75% to the final grade, and the final examination contributes 25%.
